title: The bus that never reads high
symptom: An open-collector bus line is released by its driver (the transistor turns off), but the device sampling it 100µs later keeps reading LOW. A scope on BUS shows the line crawling upward and only reaching a valid high after a few milliseconds. The transistor tests fine. The wiring matches the schematic.
instruments: Sim → Transient (try step 1e-6, stop 5e-3) and watch v(bus)
ERC (it passes — this bug is legal electricity, just wrong values)
Inspector → click components to read their values

rootCause.explanation: The pull-up has to charge the bus capacitance all by itself: τ = R·C = 100kΩ × 10nF = 1ms, so the line is nowhere near a valid high at 100µs — open-collector buses only rise as fast as their pull-up lets them. Drop the pull-up to ~4.7kΩ (τ ≈ 47µs) and the same transient shows BUS comfortably high in time. The trade: a stronger pull-up burns more current while the bus is held low — that's the real design decision, and it's why 'just copy the pull-up value' fails when bus capacitance changes.

hints: What charges the bus back to high after the transistor lets go? Nothing else is connected to it.
Estimate the RC time constant of the rise you're seeing in the transient.
Compare τ = R_pullup × C_bus against the 100µs the sampler gives you.
